basis: Function-specific textual contracts authored from the frozen executable source. Expected answers remain determined by source execution, not this text.

rules.validateSearchSynonyms:
Function contract: validateSearchSynonyms(value).
If value is omitted (undefined), return an empty list. Otherwise value must be an array of groups. An empty outer array is accepted.
Every group must be an array with at least two terms. Every term must be a string whose trimmed form consists of Unicode letters or numbers, optionally separated into words by whitespace. Empty strings and punctuation within terms are rejected.
Normalize each term by trimming it, replacing each run of whitespace with one ordinary space, and lowercasing it using the runtime locale. Normalized terms must be unique across the entire input, including within a group and between groups.
Throw if any shape, term, or uniqueness rule fails. Otherwise return the groups in their original order, with normalized terms in their original order. The question about returning normally asks whether any rule would throw.
rules.phraseMatches:
Function contract: phraseMatches(value, phrase), with string arguments.
Look for a match anywhere inside value, not necessarily the whole value. Match case-insensitively using Unicode-aware letters and numbers.
Split phrase on literal ordinary spaces. Treat every resulting word literally, including any regex punctuation inside it. Between phrase words, allow one or more whitespace characters in value.
Allow one optional literal s at the very end of the complete phrase. This suffix does not apply independently to earlier words.
Immediately before and after the whole match, require either the edge of value or a character that is neither a Unicode letter nor a Unicode number. Punctuation is therefore a boundary; an adjacent letter or number is not. Return true if at least one such match exists, otherwise false.
rules.queryUnits:
Function contract: queryUnits(query, groups). The supplied groups are lists of synonym strings.
Lowercase query using the runtime locale, split on whitespace, strip leading and trailing characters other than Unicode letters/numbers from each token, and discard empty tokens.
Create an entry for every term in every group. Split each term on ordinary spaces. Consider entries in descending number of words; ties preserve the order of terms and groups in the input.
Scan the cleaned query tokens from left to right. At each position, take the first entry whose words match the following query tokens. Each word must match exactly, except that the last word may have one extra final s.
For a matched entry, emit an object with term equal to the actual cleaned query tokens consumed, joined with ordinary spaces. This retains a plural suffix present in query. Its alternatives are all strings in that entry's group except the exact canonical entry string; preserve their order. Advance by the number of words in the match.
If no entry matches, emit the current query token with an empty alternatives list, then advance one token. Preserve repeated units and output order; do not deduplicate.
rules.validateReaderSelection:
Function contract: validateReaderSelection(value, config, where).
value must be a non-null object and must not be an array. Otherwise throw: "{where} must be a mapping of filter names to lists of choices".
For every own entry facet -> choices in value, facet must be an own property of config.facets. Otherwise throw: "{where}.{facet} is not a configured reader filter".
choices must be an array. Every choice must be a string, and config.facets[facet].options[choice] must be truthy under ordinary JavaScript property lookup. This is deliberately NOT an own-property check for option names: properties inherited from the standard Object prototype are visible. Such inherited function-valued properties are truthy. Do not trim or lowercase choice strings.
Choice strings must also be unique within that list. If the list shape, element type, truthy lookup, or uniqueness check fails, throw: "{where}.{facet} must be a unique list of configured choices".
An empty choices array is allowed. When all entries pass, return a mapping with the same facets and their unchanged lists. In error strings, replace {where} and {facet} with the actual argument and key.
rules.pageReaderFilters:
Function contract: pageReaderFilters(frontmatter, config, file).
Use JavaScript truthiness: null, undefined, false, zero, and an empty string are falsy; arrays and objects, including empty ones, are truthy.
If config is falsy, throw "{file}: readerFilters needs readerFilters.facets in the site config" when frontmatter.readerFilters is present (not undefined), even if it is null, false, or empty. Otherwise return an empty mapping. Other shorthand fields are ignored on this early-return path.
With config present, begin with explicit = an empty mapping if frontmatter.readerFilters is absent; otherwise validate that value using validateReaderSelection with where = "{file}: readerFilters". The selection rules and exact messages are given below.
If frontmatter.audiences is truthy and config.facets.audience exists, reject an own audience key in an object frontmatter.readerFilters with "{file}: use audiences or readerFilters.audience, not both". Otherwise validate {audience: frontmatter.audiences} with where = "{file}: audiences", and assign its audience list to explicit.audience. An empty audiences array still activates this step.
For product, area, and subarea, in that order: skip the facet if its frontmatter value is absent or config has no such facet. Otherwise reject an own same-named key in an object frontmatter.readerFilters with "{file}: use {facet} or readerFilters.{facet}, not both". Convert a scalar frontmatter value to a one-element array; leave an array unchanged. Validate the resulting one-facet mapping with where = "{file}: category", and assign its list into explicit.
Finally merge config.typeDefaults[frontmatter.type] (or an empty mapping if absent) with explicit. Explicit lists replace default lists for the same facet. Remove all entries whose list length is zero; do not restore a default after an empty explicit list removes it. Return the remaining mapping.
validateReaderSelection rules: its value must be a non-null non-array object or it throws "{where} must be a mapping of filter names to lists of choices". Each facet must be an own key of config.facets or it throws "{where}.{facet} is not a configured reader filter". Each choices value must be an array of unique strings, each yielding a truthy config.facets[facet].options[choice], or it throws "{where}.{facet} must be a unique list of configured choices". Empty lists are allowed. Option lookup uses ordinary JavaScript property access, including inherited prototype properties, rather than own-property membership. A valid selection returns the unchanged lists.
Replace {file}, {where}, and {facet} in error messages with the actual file argument, validation context, and facet name. Only these exact local functions are in scope; do not add broader project validation.
All explicit validation exceptions described here have name "Error" and the stated message.
